Count AWARDS when the question is how widely the buying reaches — how many firms hold a contract, whether small business is winning work, how much
administrative load a programme carries. Count DOLLARS when the question is where the money goes — market power, dependence on one supplier, exposure
if a vendor fails. A share quoted with neither base named is unreadable, and the two answers are not close: at rank 100 they are 25% and 54%.
USAspending API v2 bulk download, fetched 2026-09-22; FY2016, 554,171 awards, $125.75bn net, grouped on recipient_parent_name. CAVEAT: recipient_uei is an establishment identifier and
not a firm -- 1,299 names carry two or more of them, so UEI splits branches rather than merging spellings. These eleven civilian departments are 8.5% of federal contract awards; Defense
(68.6%) is absent, so this is not federal procurement as a whole.
